headline: Intel Has a 65% Chance of Saying Fab 28 Constrains Server Chips
deck: The desk forecasts a 65% chance Intel’s next guidance will say Fab 28 constrains server-chip availability by 31 January 2027.
body: Intel said an accident at its Israel factory had led to an extended shutdown. [E4] The paper’s 28 October coverage concerned CXMT’s reported HBM3E production; Intel’s disclosure instead quantifies a disruption at Fab 28.
The company said the factory had been shut down for about two weeks and that it expected production to start up by the end of that week. [E6]
Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion. [E1]
The company said its immediate priority was unlocking additional supply to meet extraordinary demand for its Xeon family. [E2]
Intel said it expected the PC slowdown to continue through at least the first half of next year. [E3]
The company’s fourth-quarter guidance included an early-assessment impact of roughly $300 million in revenue and 200 basis points in gross margin from the Fab 28 incident. [E5]
Intel’s 10-Q says the mid-October accident at Kiryat Gat halted manufacturing. [E7]

**The desk's reading.** The desk assigns a 65% probability that Intel will say the facility constrains server-chip availability in product or customer guidance by 31 January 2027. It starts from a neutral 50% desk prior because the reported disruption establishes neither a customer-visible constraint nor its absence, then moves up because the shutdown has lasted about two weeks, Intel has put a preliminary fourth-quarter financial impact on it, and the company says it is trying to unlock Xeon supply amid extraordinary demand. The strongest competing reading is that the restart prevents a customer-visible constraint despite the reported financial impact.

**The next test.** Intel’s public product or customer guidance through 31 January 2027 is the settlement record. A statement that Fab 28 constrains server-chip availability settles the call yes; qualifying guidance that omits that statement, or no qualifying public product or customer guidance by 31 January 2027, settles it no.

confidence.label: YES if Intel says in public product or customer guidance that Fab 28 constrains server-chip availability by 31 January 2027; NO if qualifying guidance by then omits that statement, or if Intel publishes no qualifying public product or customer guidance by 31 January 2027
